title: Speech by Chair Yellen on inflation dynamics and monetary policy - Federal Reserve Board
主要内容: On September 24, 2015, Federal Reserve Chair Janet Yellen discussed inflation dynamics and monetary policy. She noted that inflation is now more stable than in the past and is currently at a very low level. Yellen emphasized the importance of maintaining inflation close to 2 percent, highlighting the costs of high, excessively low, or unstable inflation. She reviewed historical inflation trends, noting that inflation began to rise significantly in the mid-1960s and reached very high levels during the 1970s. Core inflation, which excludes food and energy, also rose significantly during this period. Yellen pointed out that monetary policy is responsible for inflation dynamics and that the Fed was insufficiently focused on returning inflation to a predictable, low level following shocks to food and energy prices. In late 1979, the Fed began tightening monetary policy, which led to a severe economic downturn in the early 1980s. Inflation averaged less than 4% from 1983 to 1990 and then fell to about 2% for many years. Since 2009, inflation has remained below the FOMC's 2% target, partly due to a slow economic recovery.
